overview: File covers a 1945 Japanese rate increase, and 1947 coordination among SCAP, State, and the Post Office defining Japan's postal territory under SCAPIN 677 as modified.

people.name: Mrs. Buckley
people.role: Recipient of the State Department memorandum; specific position not stated

people.name: G. W. Lewis
people.role: State Department official and author of the January 28 memorandum; addressee for the attention of the Civil Affairs Division letter

people.name: Daniel Noce
people.role: Major General, General Staff Corps, and Chief of the War Department Civil Affairs Division

keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to telegram no. 810 on Japanese railway and postal rate increases
subfiles.about: The sheet cross-references a telegram reporting that Japan planned to increase railway ticket prices and postal rates from April 1.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Japan's 1945 decision to raise railway fares and postal rates effective that April.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Mrs. Buckley on the postal definition of Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum concludes that no further State Department action is needed concerning the definition of Japan for postal purposes.
subfiles.summary: Lewis tells Buckley the Post Office already has the needed information, recommending no further action.

subfiles.title: Civil Affairs Division letter defining Japan for postal purposes
subfiles.from: Major General Daniel Noce, Chief, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.to: Assistant Secretary of State J. H. Hilldring, attention G. W. Lewis
subfiles.about: The Civil Affairs Division transmits SCAP’s territorial definition of Japan and recommends its use in Post Office Department orders governing postal service.
subfiles.summary: Noce relays SCAP's 1947 postal definition of Japan's territory, excluding Korea-linked islands and the Kurils, for the Post Office.

interest: Shows 1945-47 wartime and postwar questions over Japanese postal rates and SCAP's territorial definition of Japan.
